A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transportation infrastructure should be represented in a network model, and that the network model should be augmented with additional information.

mobile data modeling is not a problem that can be solved with a single model, but rather with a set of models, each of which is tailored to a particular application domain and each of which is used for different purposes.
the key to success is to use a combination of different representations and data models, each with its own strengths and weaknesses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a holistic approach to data modeling for mobile services is needed, which integrates the transportation network with other infrastructure and content data, as well as user profiles.

the data model for mobile services is not just a database, but an integrated system that combines a variety of representations of the transportation network and the surrounding environment, with the ability to relate them to each other and to the user's location and context.
a single, unified representation of the transportation infrastructure is not sufficient to support the variety of services that can be delivered to mobile customers.
